# proc

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/proc"
```

Package proc runs supervised processes.

A process is a mutable struct that embeds Process\[A\] and has a Run\(context.Context\) method with a pointer receiver. A is the immutable argument type of the process; use None for a process without arguments. Start creates a new process value, gives it the arguments, runs Run in a new goroutine, and returns its PID. Callers keep the PID and call exported methods directly on the process pointer from PID.Proc. The immutago analyzer proves that these methods take and return only immutable values and PIDs. For processes that need each other's PIDs, Reserve a PID first and start it later with StartReserved.

A supervisor runs its children until Stop. If Run returns, the process ends. If Run panics, the supervisor waits 1 s, doubling the delay for each restart in the last 5 minutes. It then creates a new process value from the same arguments, stores it in the same PID, and calls Run. Calls during the delay still use the old value; calls already in progress finish on that value. A sixth panic from the same child in 5 minutes stops all children of the supervisor in reverse start order and escalates the panic to the parent supervisor, which restarts the subtree with the same rule. At the root supervisor, the escalation panics again with the last panic value, and the program exits. OnPanic reports each recovered panic.

Stop cancels each Run context and waits for Run to return. Cancellation is cooperative; Run must observe its context. Stop does not wait for direct method calls. Process methods must synchronize their own shared state.

## func StartReserved

```go
func StartReserved[T, A any, P interface {
    *T
    Run(context.Context)
    bind(A)
}](parent *Supervisor, pid PID[T], args A)
```

StartReserved creates a process value with args, stores it in pid, and runs its Run method under parent. The PID is started when StartReserved returns. Each restart creates a new value from the same args. If parent is stopped, the process does not run. StartReserved panics if pid is already started.

## type Dependency

Dependency holds a value that the caller trusts to be safe for concurrent use by several processes, for example a logger, an HTTP client, a factory function, or a test fake. The value is not immutable. The analyzer does not prove this trust. It permits Dependency only as a process argument type or as a named field of a marked process argument struct.

```go
type Dependency[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Trust

```go
func Trust[T any](v T) Dependency[T]
```

Trust wraps v. The call is the caller's promise that several processes can use v at the same time.

### func \(Dependency\[T\]\) Value

```go
func (d Dependency[T]) Value() T
```

Value returns the trusted value.

## type None

None is the argument type of a process without arguments.

```go
type None struct {
    im.Shared
}
```

## type Option

Option configures a root supervisor.

```go
type Option func(*Supervisor)
```

### func OnPanic

```go
func OnPanic(report func(value any, stack []byte)) Option
```

OnPanic makes report receive the value and the stack of every panic that a child of a supervisor in the tree recovers, before its restart delay. A nested supervisor that escalates is such a child of its parent.

## type PID

PID identifies a process. Start returns a started PID; Reserve returns a PID to start later.

```go
type PID[T any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func Reserve

```go
func Reserve[T any]() PID[T]
```

Reserve returns a PID that is not started. Proc panics until StartReserved starts it.

### func Start

```go
func Start[T, A any, P interface {
    *T
    Run(context.Context)
    bind(A)
}](parent *Supervisor, args A) PID[T]
```

Start reserves a PID and starts it with args under parent, as StartReserved does.

### func \(PID\[T\]\) Proc

```go
func (p PID[T]) Proc() *T
```

Proc returns the current process value with one atomic load. It panics if the PID is not started.

## type Process

Process marks a mutable struct that runs as a supervised process with arguments of type A. Only Start and StartReserved create it, and other code calls its exported methods through a PID. Embed it by value. A named field or pointer embedding does not mark the struct.

```go
type Process[A any] struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func \(\*Process\[A\]\) Args

```go
func (p *Process[A]) Args() A
```

Args returns the arguments that Start or StartReserved gave to the process.

## type Supervisor

Supervisor runs processes and nested supervisors.

```go
type Supervisor struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

### func NewRoot

```go
func NewRoot(options ...Option) *Supervisor
```

NewRoot returns a root supervisor.

### func StartSupervisor

```go
func StartSupervisor(parent *Supervisor) *Supervisor
```

StartSupervisor returns a new supervisor that parent runs as a child. When the nested supervisor's Stop channel closes, its parent has removed its child entry.

### func \(\*Supervisor\) Stop

```go
func (s *Supervisor) Stop() <-chan struct{}
```

Stop begins stopping; the channel closes when all children have stopped, last started first. Stop does not wait, so a process can stop its own supervisor from Run.
